minutes.headline: Board says the failed override is a mandate to expand commercial zoning for revenue
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board held its annual reorganization (keeping the same slate of officers and committee appointees), welcomed newly elected member Tony Niccastro, and heard the director's plan for summer working sessions on new housing and site-plan bylaws. It endorsed two ANRs, found a proposed change at 171 Arbor Street not de minimis and sent it to peer review, gave preliminary feedback on a Sunny Hill Road common driveway, continued a Unitil substation storm water hearing, and approved the Subaru dealership redevelopment at 757 Chase Road with conditions.

what_happened.line: Board members opened the meeting saying the failed override is a mandate to expand commercial zoning for revenue, before any bylaw language exists.
Board approved the Subaru dealership redevelopment at 757 Chase Road, adding conditions on vehicle loading and pre-installation soil testing.
Board found a proposed change at 171 Arbor Street not a minor (de minimis) modification and sent the storm water question to outside peer review, billed to the applicant.
Board kept its slate of officers and committee appointees unchanged for the year and continued three other pending site applications to June 22.

why_it_matters: The board's stated reading of the override result could shape future proposals to rezone land for commercial use, which would affect where new business development is allowed in town.
The Chase Road approval and the Arbor Street peer-review referral affect what conditions nearby residents can expect on drainage, traffic and site work for those specific projects.
Three pending applications (30 Summer Street, 10 Parmentor Road, 860 New West Townsend Road) and the Unitil substation storm water hearing move to June 22, when residents can next weigh in.
